title: Stalk of a direct image of sets as sections over the strict henselization
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $H$ a sheaf of sets on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets] with direct image $f_*H$, $(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$ for $V$ in $Y_{\Et}$, and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ be the category of affine pointed etale neighbourhoods $(V,\bar v)$ of $\bar y$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], $V=\operatorname{Spec}A_V$, and let $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}=\varinjlim_{(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}}A_V$, $Y^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with the canonical morphisms $c_V:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V$ (induced by the coprojections $A_V\to C$) and $q:Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y$ (the composite of $c_V$ with $V\to Y$, independent of $V$). Let $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\times_YX$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $f^{\mathrm{sh}}:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to Y^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $p:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to X$, let $p^{-1}H$ be the etale inverse image of sheaves of sets and $p^*s\in(p^{-1}H)(W\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}})$, for $W$ in $X_{\Et}$ and $s\in H(W)$, the image of $s$ under the unit $H\to p_*p^{-1}H$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units]. For $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ let $\sigma_V:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to(V\times_YX)\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}}$ be the morphism with components $(c_V\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}},p):X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V\times_YX$ and $\mathrm{id}:X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to X^{\mathrm{sh}}$; it is a morphism of $X^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] from the final object $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ to the object $(V\times_YX)\times_XX^{\mathrm{sh}}\xrightarrow{\mathrm{pr}_2}X^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Then: (1) every element of the stalk $(f_*H)_{\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is the germ of a section at an affine pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar y$; (2) there is exactly one map of sets $\Theta:(f_*H)_{\bar y}\to(p^{-1}H)(X^{\mathrm{sh}})$ such that for every $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal N^{\mathrm{aff}}$ and every $s\in(f_*H)(V)=H(V\times_YX)$, $\Theta(\text{germ of }s\text{ at }(V,\bar v))=(p^{-1}H)(\sigma_V)(p^*s)$; and $\Theta$ is bijective.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), case n = 0, for sheaves of sets (the case used in the proof of Proposition Tag 03QP (1)): proof, 'We may replace I by the initial subcategory consisting of affine etale neighbourhoods ... Spec(O^sh) = lim V ... X x_S Spec(O^sh) = lim X x_S V', concluded in degree 0 for sheaves of sets by Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit) / Lemma Tag 09YU (lemma-category-is-colimit) on global sections

proof.text: Let $\mathcal J$ be the small cofiltered representative category used in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and write $X_V=V\times_YX$ for $(V,\bar v)\in\mathcal J$. Since $V$ is affine and $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives that $X_V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The category $\mathcal J$ need not be a preorder, so apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] to the filtered category $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$: we obtain a nonempty directed set $A$, objects $(V_a,\bar v_a)$ of $\mathcal J$ and morphisms $V_b\to V_a$ of $\mathcal J$ for $a\le b$, compatible with composition, such that by its clause (2) the cone $(Y^{\mathrm{sh}},(c_{V_a})_a)$ obtained from the limit cone of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] is a limit of the inverse system $(V_a)_{a\in A}$, and by its clause (1) every colimit of a functor $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ is the colimit of its restriction to $A$; put $X_a=X_{V_a}$. Each transition $X_b\to X_a$ is affine by base change of the affine map $V_b\to V_a$. The limit description [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] and the affine Spec colimit-limit identification [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit], together with the universal property of fibre products, identify $X^{\mathrm{sh}}=Y^{\mathrm{sh}}\times_YX$ with $\varprojlim_{a\in A}X_a$ and identify its projection to $X_a$ with $(c_{V_a}\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}},p):X^{\mathrm{sh}}\to V_a\times_YX$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, passage Spec(O^sh)=lim V and X x_Y Spec(O^sh)=lim (X x_Y V)

proof.text: Apply the new continuity node [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-section-continuity] to the directed system $X_a=X_{V_a}$, the limit $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$, the sheaf $G=\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}^{-1}H$ on $(X_{V_0})_{\Et}$, and $W_0=X_{V_0}$ with its identity etale morphism. The hypotheses hold because the $X_a$ are qcqs with affine transitions by step 1; the base changes $W_a$ are $X_{V_a}$, and the transition maps are precisely the unit, the composition isomorphism $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units], and restriction along the iterated-fibre-product isomorphism. The node gives $\varinjlim_a(f_{a0}^{-1}G)(X_{V_a})\xrightarrow{\sim}(f_0^{-1}G)(X^{\mathrm{sh}})$. Since $\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}\circ f_{a0}=\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}$ and $\operatorname{pr}_{V_0}\circ f_0=p$ (step 1), the isomorphisms $c$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identify $f_{a0}^{-1}G$ with $\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}^{-1}H$ and $f_0^{-1}G$ with $p^{-1}H$, so the node gives $\varinjlim_a(\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}^{-1}H)(X_{V_a})\xrightarrow{\sim}(p^{-1}H)(X^{\mathrm{sh}})$. The projection $\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}:X_{V_a}\to X$ is etale (base change of the etale $V_a\to Y$), so [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-restriction] gives $\rho:(\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}^{-1}H)(X_{V_a})\xrightarrow{\sim}H(X_{V_a})$, under which the unit $\operatorname{pr}_{V_a}^*$ is restriction (its clause (2)); with clauses (0)-(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] this turns the transition map $\rho_{ba}$ into the restriction map $H(X_{V_a})\to H(X_{V_b})$ of $f_*H$ along $X_{V_b}\to X_{V_a}$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal] (step 1), $\varinjlim_{a\in A}H(X_{V_a})$ is the colimit of $H(X_V)$ over $\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}$, the affine-neighbourhood colimit.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9, degree zero, using Theorem Tag 09YQ (theorem-colimit) and Lemma Tag 09YU (lemma-category-is-colimit)

proof.text: Under the identification in steps 1-2, the map from the $V_a$-component of the section colimit is exactly restriction along $\sigma_{V_a}$ of the unit image $p^*s$: the component of $\sigma_{V_a}$ over $V_a\times_YX$ is $c_{V_a}\circ f^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and its component over $X^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is the identity. Clauses (0)-(1) of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] identify this restriction with $(p^{-1}H)(\sigma_{V_a})(p^*s)$, and their composition and unit identities show compatibility for maps of pointed neighbourhoods. Cofinality transports the formula from the $V_a$ to every $V\in\mathcal J$. Thus the bijection of step 2 induces the unique map $\Theta$ with the displayed component formula.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, identification of the degree-zero colimit map with restriction of the unit section

proof.text: By the definition of the geometric stalk as the filtered colimit over all pointed etale neighbourhoods, and the initiality of the affine subcategory [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], the stalk $(f_*H)_{\bar y}$ is canonically the colimit of the sets $H(V\times_YX)$ over $V\in\mathcal J$. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal], the directed family $A$ from step 1 computes the same colimit. The map of step 3 consequently has domain $(f_*H)_{\bar y}$, proves clause (1) (every germ has an affine representative), and is bijective by step 2, proving clause (2).
